2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 General - The meat used for canning shall be of good quality, obtained from the carcasses of only heal[hy ammals, slaughtered in licensed premises, and subjected to proper ante-mortem and post-mortem inspection as prescribed in IS: 1982-1972*. and Workmanship

2.2 Material

2.2.1 He:xl meat, scrap meat, meat siianks, end of plates shall not bc canned.

flanks and

skirts

and

navel

2.2.2 The set mwt shall bc freed from bones, blood clots, bruised material, all skin, hair, stringy 2nd fibrous tissue, tendons and excessive Fasciae and depot fat shall be separafat. Viscera shall not be canned. ted, as far as possible.

2.2.3 After setting, the material shall be cut into chunks or cuboids of `l'he chunks shall be dry-cured by sprinkling with 2.5 to 4 cm dimensions. a mixture of sodium nitrale and sodium nitrite or ascorbic acid of such concentration as to ensure a desirC~ble coiour to the meat. The chunks may aljo be cure:-l by any other approved pr')ccss for any length of time, subject to an agreement between the purchaser and the vendor. 2.3 Freedom

other than sodium 2.4 Preservatives - Preservatives, nitrate of sodium and potassium, shall not be used.

2.5 Tenderizing Material - Tenderizing material, either artificial, to soften meat before processing, shall not be used.

2.6 The material shall be of a good flavour and shall have the characteristic flavour, typical -of good canned meat. It shall be free from any objectionable odour or colour. 2.7 Hygienic

IS : 1743 - 1973 2.8 Requirements for the Finished Product

2.8.1 The contents of the can on opening shall not display disintegration. Excessive separation of muscle fibres resulting in a fiuffy suspension shall be considered as disintegration. 2.8.2 The canned meat shall have characteristic colour and flavour.

2.8.3 The material shall be free from pieces of bristle, hair, skin and particles of bone. It shall be free from dirt, insect or rodent contamination or any other extraneous matter. 2.8.4 Poisonous and deleterious substances of microbiological origin shall not be present. of any type including those

PROCEDURE

D-3.1 Transfer a lo-ml aliquot of the test solution ( see B-3.1 ) to a separating funnel. Add one gram of citric acid and dissolve it by shaking. Make the solution alkaline to litmus by adding ammonium hydroxide solution in small quantities. Add 5 ml of the sodium diethyldithiocarbamate solution, shake thoroughly and extract with 5-ml portions of carbon tetrachloride until the fiilal extract is colourless. Dry the combined Filter extracts by shakrng thoroughly with anhydrous sodium sulphate. the dry extract and wash the filter paper with carbon tetrachloride. Make up the volume of the filtrate to 25 ml with carbon tetrachloride and measure the absorption at 437 nm by means of the spectrophotometer. Simultaneously carry out blank determinations on the water and the: reagents. D-3.2 Prepare a series of standards by treating aliquots of the standard copper solution ( see D-2.7 ) in the same manner as the test solution. From tile absorption of the standard solutions, prepare a standard curve plotting absorption values against concentration. From the curve, obtain the mass of copper present in the test solution.

PROCEDURE

F-2.1 Take a suitable aliquot of the test solution (see B-3.1 ), dilrlte to 460 ml, cool and add ammonium hydroxide solution until the cc,ntcnts are alkaline. Add 20 ml of either conccntratcd hydrochloric acid or Cover the beaker wirh a watch glass. Heat the dilute sulphuric acid. solution to about 95�C and pac.s a slow stream of llydrogen sulphidc gas Digest the mixture at 95�C for one hour and through it for one hour. allow it to stand for another 30 minutes. Filter the contents of the beaker through a quantitative filter paper and wash the rc,sidue of stannous with three portions eacl; of wash solution sulphide on the filter, alternately and hot water. Transfer the rcidue alon (: with tbc filter paper to a 5O_ml beaker, add 10 to 20 ml of ammonium polysulphide rolution, lieat Add 10 ml Lf ammonium p~lystllto boilirjg and filtc r by decantation; Repcat this once more and finally phide solution, I,oil and filLer again. Acidify the combined filtrate alld wash the filter paper with hot water. washings with dilute acetic acid, gently boil for or:e hour and allow to E ilter the rcsultmg mixture through a double 11-cm stand overnight. &less filter paper. Wash the filter paper alternately with two portions 19

Is 11743- 1973
each of the wash solution and hot water. Transfer the residue along with the titer paper to a tared porcelain crucible and dry it thoroughly in an air oven. Carefully ignite the filter paper, using a Bunsen flame and incinerate the contents to convert the sulphide to oxide. Partly cover the crucible and heat strongly over a Bunsen or Meker burner. ( The sulphide shall be gently roasted to the oxide which may then be heated to a high temperature without loss by volatilization. ) F-2.2 Cool the crucible in a desiccator and weigh as stanruc oxide ( SnO, ). Repeat the process of heating, cooling and weighing till the difference between two successive weighings is less than one milligram. Note the lowest mass. Obtain the mass of metallic tin from the weight of stannic oxide ( SnO, ) by using the factor g-T87 7.

IS : 1743 - 1973

G-5.2.1 This recording is done preferably with an electric recording type of instrument without opening the can. If such an instrument is not available, the recording may be done with a vacuum-pressure gauge of the piercing type. G-5.2.2 sterilized
Recording of Vacuum or Pressure with a Vacuum-Pressure Gauge

G-5.2.2.1

The site of the opening to be made by any of the following methods:

aj Pour ethyl alcohol ( 95 percent ), freely on the top-end plate and Flame the petri dish freely and close the end plate with set fire. the dish immediately after the alcohol has burnt down. b) Hoid the can in the hand and heat the end plate freely in a Bunsen flame waving the end plate against the flame with a circular motion so as to protect the contents against scorching. Cover with a sterile petri dish as before. c) In case the can is bulged, it is not safe to directly flame it. It can be sterilized by swabbing freely with a mixture of ethyl alcohol ( 98 percent ) and chloroform or formaldehyde after washing with soap and water. G-5.2.2.2 After flaming, allow the can to remain under the sterile petri dish until quite cool ( 30 minutes would do) and then pierce the point of opening by means of a sterile vacuum-pressure gauge of the piercing type Record the vacuum or positive pressure as the under aseptic conditions. case may be. Cover the opening immediately after removing the vacuumpressure gauge. G-5.3 Preparation of the Sample for Bacteriological TestsEnlarge under aseptic conditions the puncture with a thoroughly sterilized If a cutting type of can-opener to give an opening of 2.5 cm diameter. instrument is used, cut a triangle with a base of 2.5 cm and sides 5 cm long. Cover the enlarged opening at once with sterile petri dish. G-5.4 Removal of the Inoculum

G-5.4.1 Removal of Liquid Inoculum - The inoculum is especially removed 1,); means of a sterile pipette graduated in millilitres. It is essential that the rear end of the pipette be plugged for a length not less than I.5 cm Lvith sterile cotton wool. Deliver 2 ml of the inoculum to each of the broth tubes and one millilitre to each of the melted agar tubes. Mix well to ensure uniform distribution and pour into the petri dishes, swirling so ;IS to obtain uniform spread. AlternativeIy, pour 2 ml of the inoculum 27

IS : 1743 - 1973 into the petri swirling. dish and then add the melted agar medium and rnix bv

G-5.4.2 Removal of Solid lnoculum - For removing the samples of solid material, use sterile cork-borers or sample tubes or spoons. If spoons are used, the content5 of the can should be thoroughly mixed before taking the sample. Remove abnut 15 g of the sample and transfer it IO a sterile flask containin? 50 ml of sterile water or sterile normal saline or sterile Ringers solution. The Aask should contain at least a dozen sterile glass beads to faciiitate mixing. Mix by swirling for at least 5 minutes. Take out Z-ml portions of the inoculum and add them to `both the broths and the agars. G-5.5 Preparation of the Anaerobic Culture - The dextrose-tryplonebroth and the liver-broth media are rendered anaerobic by sealing the access to air by placing a layer of sterile Vaseline, liquid paraffin, iiquid agar or paraffin lvax on the top of the medium. This layer should be not less than 1.5 cm in thickness. J ust b e f ore using the culture tubes, exhaust the media by packing the tubes for at least IO minutes in a lvater-bath and maintain the lvarer-bath at 70�C until the media are used. Inoculate the medium below the paraffin agar layer with as little disturbance as possible and cool the medium after inoculation in a cold water-bath so that the top seal is set.
